title: Choose the visual world for Shoot Project (re-roll 1)
question: A fresh hand, steered warm, human and premium. Everything shown before (The Shoot Pass, Bilingual Wayfinding and their challengers) is out. Keep the roll, take another, or re-roll.

options.label: The Set Menu
options.lineage: Dubai hotel restaurant set menus: courses, 'choose one', a fixed price at the foot
options.thesis: Your brief is a set menu: six courses, choose one of each, and the price is settled before you sit down.
materials: no folder, no tassel: only the menu's grammar
options.viewport: Phone: a quiet top bar on warm plaster, then one pomegranate menu card that is the page: 'You brief. We shoot.' as the menu head with its Arabic line beside it, six courses (small-caps head, the chosen dish large, a dotted leader to 'change'), the fixed-price line at the foot, and the action 'See who's free' as a full-width cacao bar printed on the card. Desktop: the same single tall card centred on the plaster ground, never a split hero.
options.risk: If the card is set like a restaurant pastiche it becomes a costume; set like a serious modern menu it is simply a warm, exact page. The 'fixed price' line must stay honest while no price exists.

raised.raise: The six courses are identical units in one rhythm, so the eye sweeps the whole brief in one pass instead of opening each line.
State lives in the material: a set course prints in full rice-white, an unset one waits in muted ink, with no icons to decode.
No decorative greys: every tone on the card has one job, and the only warm accent marks the course you are choosing now.
A choice, once made, stays printed on the page; nothing collapses into a chip, and the confirmation is the same card marked served.
One direction of travel: head, courses, price, action; no sideways competition anywhere in the first viewport.

options.label: The Credit Line
options.lineage: fashion-magazine shoot credits, as in Vogue Arabia spreads: the plate, then 'Photographer, Location, Date'
options.thesis: Your brief is the credit line of a shoot that has not happened yet, printed under the plate that is waiting for the picture.
options.viewport: Phone: the masthead, then a tall plate that owns the top half as an honest colour field labelled for the shoot that goes there, the headline set across its lower edge, the six credits beneath as 'Photographer / Occasion / Date / Duration / Emirate / Shot by', and the action as a bold rule-bar. Desktop: one spread, plate on the start page, credits on the end page.
options.risk: The familiar destination: editorial is where most runs in this category land, and it needs real photography to sing; until then the plate is a colour field with a promise on it.

options.label: Dawn Cyc
options.lineage: a seamless theatre cyclorama lit from night through cobalt and rose into white day
options.thesis: The page starts in night; each line of the brief you set lifts the horizon, and the action stands in full daylight.
options.viewport: Phone: depthless black at the top with the headline in white, a cobalt band holding the six brief lines as cues, a rose band gathering above the white-day band where the action waits; as lines are set the day rises up the screen.
options.case: Fuses well: the brief as cues that bring up the day is a true state language and the action stands in the lit band; loses identification, since stage lighting is backstage craft, not the client's world.
options.risk: If the bands blur into a gradient it becomes the glowing-edge dark template; the bands must stay flat and exact.

options.label: Akari Lanterns
options.lineage: washi over bamboo ribs, lit from inside
options.thesis: Each line of the brief is a paper lantern that lights when set.
options.viewport: Glowing paper volumes hanging at different heights, unlit ones folded flat.
options.case: Warm and premium, but UAE clients do not identify with Japanese lanterns, and glowing paper lowers text contrast on a phone.
options.risk: Soft glow becomes a blurry template.
options.kept: State carried by material, not icons.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: The brief as a strobing data field.
options.viewport: A wall of hairline bars with numbers in the margin.
options.case: The opposite of the steer: cold, abstract, hostile to a wedding client and to Arabic text.
options.risk: Strobing fails reduced motion and accessibility.
options.kept: No decorative greys; every tone has a job.

options.label: VU-meter Bridge
options.lineage: a row of ballistic needles across a recording desk
options.thesis: Six needles that lean into the red as the brief fills.
options.viewport: A row of identical meters above the brief.
options.case: Warm materials, but a recording desk is a studio tool; clients do not identify with it and needles do not explain a choice.
options.kept: Identical repeated units read as one ruler.

options.label: Torn Billboard
options.lineage: Paris hoardings torn through to earlier posters
options.thesis: The brief revealed by tearing layers.
options.viewport: Fragments of four type systems at four scales.
options.case: Illegible by design and anti-premium; fails both axes for a client who wants to book in a minute.
options.risk: Reads as decoration with no offer.
options.kept: A choice once made stays on the page as a record.

options.label: Pulp Rocket Plate
options.lineage: pulp magazine rocket plates on a diagonal
options.thesis: The brief as a flight path.
options.viewport: A craft crossing on a diagonal with porthole controls.
options.case: Nostalgic sci-fi has no home with UAE wedding and brand clients, and diagonals fight Arabic reading order.
options.kept: One direction of travel through the page.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A premium photography booking site: moody full-bleed photo, serif headline, booking widget on top.
canonCard.viewport: Dark photo hero, large serif line, the brief sentence in a rounded card with an amber button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from shootix.ae and every studio site, and it needs real photography you do not have yet.
